slides.title: Connecting Daily Work to the Bigger Picture
bullets: Strategic thinking links daily, operational work to the broader business and product picture
It separates those who just execute tasks from those who anticipate and prioritize
The focus stays on what matters over the medium and long term

slides.title: Understand the Business Behind the Science
bullets: Know how drug development gets financed and how patent timing drives decisions
Understand access and reimbursement dynamics in relevant markets
Know the role each function plays across commercial, market access, regulatory and pharmacovigilance
This cross-functional fluency makes the medical voice more persuasive in strategy discussions

slides.title: Tie Every Activity to the Medical Plan
bullets: Before investing time, ask how the activity serves the cycle's top medical priorities
Applies to KOL relationships, congress coverage and insight work alike
The alternative is operating purely reactively to whatever comes up

slides.title: Anticipate Before Signals Become Facts
bullets: Watch for early signals: competitive shifts, emerging trends, regulatory changes under discussion
Think through the implications ahead of time rather than reacting once they're settled
This builds directly on the medical listening and intelligence practices from earlier modules

slides.title: Deciding With Incomplete Information
bullets: Prioritize among reasonable alternatives when there is no obviously correct answer
This is developed through deliberate practice on real decisions, not theory alone

slides.title: A Discipline, Refined Daily
bullets: Strategic thinking is not reserved for people already in director roles
It is practiced and refined in every everyday decision
Professionals who build it early consistently reach strategic responsibility faster

takeaway.title: Strategic thinking turns daily execution into a deliberate contribution to the bigger picture
bullets: Business fluency lets the medical voice land more persuasively in strategy conversations
Tie every activity back to the Medical Plan's top priorities instead of reacting
Anticipating signals and deciding with incomplete information are trainable, practiced skills
